The pair64 ownership probe preserved the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 WMMA shape but remapped two wave32 waves to one Vulkan-style 64x64 output owner, matching the specialized Vulkan coopmat ownership more closely than the previous 16x128 wave striping. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=25, VGPR=134, LDS=20480) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 12 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, and 28 s_waitcnts. The true wave64 WMMA probe used the ROCm __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16_w64 builtin rather than compiling the wave32 builtin in wave64 mode. It follows the AMD matrix-instruction-calculator RDNA3 mapping for A/B fragments and D stores, preserves the VK128 padded direct-F32 shape, and compiles through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=165, LDS=20480). The explicit ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape, direct F32 RHS, and ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin while forcing A/B LDS fragment reads through inline assembly. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=30, VGPR=169, LDS=20480, no spills, 256 ds_load_b64 sites, 0 ds_load_b128 sites, 32 static WMMA sites, 396 s_waitcnts, and 2 barriers. The grouped ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape and explicit LDS b64 fragment reads, but changed the compute window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half before issuing the 4x4 WMMA block. A no-wait grouping emitted the same 64 ds_load_b64 class but failed focused p512/p513 correctness with NaNs. The conservative waited grouping selected correctly for p512 and p513, kept exact p33 on the narrow Q4 route, and passed focused CPU-reference gates for p512, p33, and p513. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row Kcur p512 perf regressed badly versus the current MMQL128 baseline under the same runner and explicit baseline gate: 1038.69 us for MMQL128 versus 3103.19 us for B64GROUP. Matching RADV's LDS load count and 4x4 fragment reuse is therefore not enough while the HIP inline-asm wait schedule and direct-F32 WMMA dataflow remain far from the RADV cooperative-matrix schedule.

The B-oct packed-Q8_1/x4 probe mechanically brackets the only positive post-oracle Q4 packed-path axis. It preserves the accepted MMQL128/B-quad dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but preloads all eight WNITER B-cache positions before issuing the dot loop. This tests whether a broader post-barrier B-cache LDS read window can move further toward the RADV oracle after B-pair and B-quad improved full-tile model rows. It built through CMake/Ninja, but compile evidence rejects it before runtime: wave64, SGPR=53, VGPR=192, LDS=8192, private_segment_fixed_size=376, and vgpr_spill_count=94 with scratch load/store traffic in the ISA. Keep B-quad as the current no-spill default; B-oct exceeds the gfx1151 resource envelope.

The B-quad-CR packed-Q8_1/x4 probe preserves the accepted B-quad B-cache cluster size and MMQL128 dataflow, but changes consume order so each A micro-row drains the loaded B cluster before moving to the next A row. This tests wait/issue order with B-quad-level live state after B-oct proved the full B window spills. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=53, VGPR=167, LDS=8192, no spills, which is slightly lower register pressure than accepted B-quad. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed. Keep accepted B-quad; CR consume order drains waits differently but loses the rows that dominate model throughput.

This matches RADV's 32 WMMA and 64 ds_load_b64 axes and moves the store count from the accepted default's 64 to 128, but it still misses RADV's 22528-byte LDS footprint, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 LDS b16 stores, and 192 buffer stores. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513 with the candidate selected. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed every row versus the accepted default: p33 Vcur 678.53 -> 798.70 us, ffn_out 3266.17 -> 3836.85 us, result_output 17918.60 -> 23491.26 us; p512 Vcur 1229.96 -> 2383.51 us, ffn_out 22244.78 -> 28722.42 us, result_output 180519.25 -> 232795.11 us; p513 Vcur 1031.38 -> 1138.76 us, ffn_out 12337.31 -> 16923.53 us, result_output 112612.90 -> 135186.16 us. Combining the source-visible b64 load and fullstore writeback pivots is still not the Vulkan cooperative-matrix load/store/lane-ownership schedule.

The b64group-store-stage Q6_K direct-F32 WMMA probe combined the remaining source-visible RADV axes after isolated B64GROUP, FULLSTORE, STORE_STAGE, and B64GROUP_FULLSTORE probes failed: grouped ds_read_b64 fragment loads plus explicit LDS output staging. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=196, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16, 66 ds_store_b16, 64 global_store_b32, 34 barriers, and 367 s_waitcnt. This matches RADV's large-route tile, LDS footprint, 32 WMMA, and 64 ds_load_b64 axes, but still misses RADV's 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 LDS b16 stores, 192 buffer stores, and two-barrier cooperative-matrix writeback. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513; p33 stayed on the accepted VK64 narrow route, while p512 and p513 selected the candidate. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed every production-width row versus the accepted default: p512 Vcur 1253.70 -> 2442.08 us, ffn_out 22306.27 -> 28932.14 us, result_output 182744.78 -> 230756.64 us; p513 Vcur 1041.04 -> 1151.76 us, ffn_out 11754.13 -> 16996.90 us, result_output 110050.98 -> 136412.67 us. Combining the visible HIP C++ b64-load and output-stage pivots is still not the Vulkan cooperative-matrix load/store/lane-ownership schedule.

The BN128 split-qsum8 packed-Q8_1 probe preserved the accepted BN128 full-column policy and changed only the qsum chunk size from 16 columns to 8 columns. This was a bounded live-range/occupancy probe after accepted BN128 split-qsum removed the old simple-BN128 spill wall. It compiled through CMake/Ninja and achieved the intended resource effect: wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=120, LDS=4352, no spills, versus accepted BN128 split-qsum VGPR=152. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; route traces proved p33 stayed on BN64 while p512 and p513 selected split-qsum8 under the opt-in env. Same-runner focused timing rejects it for production: p512 improved Vcur 541.25 -> 538.38 us, Qcur 1874.22 -> 1778.22 us, and ffn_out 7048.63 -> 6558.90 us, but regressed ffn_gate 6303.30 -> 6843.30 us and the dominant result_output 56355.07 -> 61269.62 us. p513 regressed every row: Vcur 537.46 -> 557.28 us, Qcur 2040.09 -> 2183.83 us, ffn_out 7958.16 -> 8170.67 us, ffn_gate 7449.29 -> 7793.47 us, and result_output 64570.31 -> 71864.74 us. Lower VGPR alone is not enough; the extra chunk-loop overhead and changed scheduling lose the rows that dominate model throughput.

The BM32/BN128 packed-Q8_1 probe preserved BN128 full-column coverage but changed output ownership from the accepted BM64/COLS32 split-qsum route to BM32/COLS16 with a simple qsum tile. This was a bounded register-tile/output-ownership test after Q8_0 remained the worst post-BN128 basket row. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=135, LDS=4352, no spills, improving compile pressure versus accepted BN128 split-qsum's VGPR=152. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513; route traces proved p33 stayed on the narrow/default path while p512 and p513 selected the candidate under the opt-in env. Same-runner focused timing rejects it for production because every p512 and p513 row regressed versus the current default: p512 Vcur 550.04 -> 625.05 us, Qcur 1882.69 -> 2087.72 us, ffn_out 7043.92 -> 8482.13 us, ffn_gate 6416.43 -> 7242.67 us, result_output 55913.71 -> 64160.60 us; p513 Vcur 531.02 -> 717.80 us, Qcur 2018.92 -> 2432.01 us, ffn_out 7762.03 -> 9816.67 us, ffn_gate 7209.13 -> 8530.12 us, result_output 63218.36 -> 76252.10 us. Reducing per-thread columns while keeping BN128 loses row-tile amortization and does not recover the missing Vulkan schedule.

The Q8_0 VK128 buffer-store probe replaced both full-tile and guarded edge writeback with __builtin_amdgcn_raw_buffer_store_b32 while preserving the direct-F32 VK128 W64 math path and the stage-allocation LDS footprint. The original gfx1151 descriptor word 0x27000 was wrong: a CMake/Ninja-built raw-buffer-store fixture showed it effectively no-ops, while the Tensile gfx11 resource word 0x31004000 passes both make_buffer_rsrc and manual descriptors on production-sized 4096x512, 14336x512, and 128256x512 output shapes. With the route patched to use 0x31004000, focused CPU-reference gates passed for p512 and p513 selected large rows, while p33 correctly stayed on the narrow packed route. The route is still rejected for production because same-runner focused timing regressed versus current default routing on every selected large row: p512 ffn_out 7048.33 -> 10357.40 us, ffn_gate 6358.83 -> 10973.75 us, result_output 56008.26 -> 98015.71 us; p513 ffn_out 7611.67 -> 10779.03 us, ffn_gate 6875.18 -> 13367.04 us, result_output 62863.76 -> 111411.43 us. Correct raw buffer stores are therefore a necessary primitive, not the Vulkan-winning schedule. The next exact-schedule attempt must reproduce RADV's cooperative-matrix load/store lane ownership and halfword LDS topology, not just the buffer-store opcode.

The Q5_K packed-Q8_1/x4 CR issue-order probe preserved BM128/BN128/WG256/wave64/BK_STEP1 and changed only the inner dot issue order to consume one Q5 row cache across columns before advancing cr. It compiled through CMake/Ninja but spilled badly (wave64, SGPR=50, VGPR=192, LDS=10240, private_segment_fixed_size=452, vgpr_spill_count=135) while preserving 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8, 64 global_store_b32, and 2 barriers. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; p512 selected CR for Qcur/ffn_out/ffn_gate, p33 stayed on rows2/MMQ64, and p513 fell back to current MMQL128 for tails. It is rejected because same-runner p512 focused timing regressed Qcur 1225.57 -> 3832.51 us, ffn_out 7453.69 -> 21017.01 us, and ffn_gate 7161.45 -> 19333.78 us. The issue-order axis increases live ranges/spills and should not be continued without a different B ownership/prefetch strategy.

The Q5_K B64GROUP store-batch8 direct-WMMA probe preserved the closest rejected direct-F32 B64GROUP store-stage math/load schedule and changed the writeback staging granularity from one LDS stage plus two barriers per tile to one stage plus two barriers per eight tiles. This mechanically targeted the RADV low-barrier cooperative-store axis. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=214, LDS=36864, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 66 ds_store_b16, 64 global_store_b32, and 6 s_barrier. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; p33 stayed on rows2, while p512 and p513 selected batch8 for all rows. It is rejected because same-runner focused timing regressed p512 Kcur 864.14 -> 1043.49 us, Qcur 1223.22 -> 2499.40 us, ffn_out 7229.01 -> 17649.52 us, ffn_gate 6903.14 -> 16915.11 us, and p513 Kcur 886.35 -> 960.72 us, Qcur 1585.01 -> 3389.07 us, ffn_out 9601.19 -> 23409.53 us, ffn_gate 8720.37 -> 20101.28 us. Lowering barriers from 34 to 6 is still not the Vulkan schedule without RADV's cooperative-matrix store/lane ownership and 192 buffer_store_b32 writeback shape.

The Q5_K B64GROUP bufferstore direct-WMMA probe ported the known-good gfx11 raw-buffer-store primitive from Q8_0 to Q5_K and combined it with grouped LDS fragment reads. It directly tested the RADV buffer_store_b32 opcode class without adding manual LDS store-stage barriers. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=198, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_u16_d16, 2 ds_store_b16, 128 buffer_store_b32, 0 global_store_b32, and 2 barriers. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; p33 stayed on rows2, while p512 and p513 selected the bufferstore route for all rows. It is rejected because same-runner focused timing regressed p512 Kcur 871.11 -> 1038.82 us, Qcur 1232.52 -> 2388.60 us, ffn_out 7322.86 -> 17957.57 us, ffn_gate 7126.12 -> 16776.44 us, and p513 Kcur 897.54 -> 959.48 us, Qcur 1590.42 -> 3315.05 us, ffn_out 9404.53 -> 23052.67 us, ffn_gate 8409.39 -> 20001.36 us. Matching buffer_store_b32 plus B64GROUP loads is not enough without RADV's cooperative-matrix store/lane ownership and halfword LDS topology.

Follow-up after the earlier rocWMMA-unavailable note found rocWMMA headers in /srv/vm-shared/rocm/rocm-7.14.0a20260610 and proved they can compile against the active /srv/vm-shared/rocm/rocm-head compiler for gfx1151 when used from scratch. A minimal default accumulator store plus f16 WMMA fixture compiled only as wave32; forcing -mwavefrontsize64 failed because the generated rocWMMA path called the wave32 WMMA builtin without the required wave32 target feature. The extracted gfx1151 code object emitted wavefront_size=32, v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16, global_load_b128 for A/B, and eight global_store_b32 per 16x16 accumulator wave. That default store lane map matches the existing HRX wave32 helper shape (row = lane>>4 + 2*i, col = lane&15, even accumulator elements), so it does not expose a simple lane-coordinate fix. Attempting a cooperative accumulator fragment with fragment_scheduler::coop_row_major_2d also failed at template compile time: rocWMMA reports accumulator cooperative fragments as unsupported/invalid for this path. Decision: keep this as environment and ISA evidence, not a production route. The remaining Vulkan large aligned direct-WMMA delta is still the RADV cooperative-matrix global store/load/lane-ownership lowering for the 128x128 family; source-visible HIP C++ scalar/fullstore/store-stage variants have already failed to recover it.

The fast-half fullpair bufferstore compile-contract probe combined the two source-visible primitives isolated from the RADV Q8_0 large oracle: real-kernel fullpair raw-buffer writeback reaching 192 buffer_store_b32 with two barriers, and low-barrier halfword LDS topology reaching 128 ds_load_u16_d16. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=195, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 130 ds_store_b16, 192 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This is the closest current direct-WMMA convergence to the RADV schedule, passing the strict contract on WMMA count, grouped LDS loads, halfword LDS loads, buffer-store count, LDS bytes, barrier count, and spills. It is still rejected before runtime because the strict contract misses two ds_store_b16 sites and three VGPRs versus the RADV target, and the fullpair accumulator-half mapping is diagnostic rather than a correctness candidate. The extra ds_store_b16 sites appear before the final output-stage loop, so the next attempt should preserve the matched final-store surface while reducing prewrite staging/live range pressure.

The pack-stage fast-half fullpair bufferstore compile-contract probe preserved the prior fast-half output/writeback path and changed only A/B LDS staging from scalar half stores to packed ds_write_b32 pair stores. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 2 ds_store_b32, 192 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This is the first Q8_0 direct-WMMA HIP C++ object to match the selected RADV large-oracle opcode/LDS/barrier/spill contract exactly, but it is rejected before runtime because the strict resource contract still misses VGPR by four registers (196 vs RADV 192). The next attempt should preserve the pack-stage opcode surface and reduce real live range or accumulator/output ownership pressure.

The pack-stage dummy-half pressure bracket preserved the exact opcode contract from pack-stage fast-half but stored accumulator values directly after issuing the 128 ds_load_u16_d16 instructions, testing whether consuming halfword reload values caused the remaining VGPR pressure. It still compiled at VGPR=196 with no spills while preserving 32 WMMA, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 192 buffer_store_b32, 22528 LDS bytes, and two barriers. It is rejected before runtime because it proves the pressure is not caused by halfword reload consumption and the route is diagnostic rather than semantically correct.

The pack-stage fast-half launch-bounds pressure bracket preserved the exact opcode contract and changed only the kernel annotation to __launch_bounds__(256, 2). It still compiled at VGPR=196 with no spills while preserving 32 WMMA, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 192 buffer_store_b32, 22528 LDS bytes, and two barriers. It is rejected before runtime because a compiler occupancy hint does not reduce the remaining four-register pressure gap; the next attempt needs a source-level live-range or ownership change.

The stream-column pack-stage fast-half probe preserved the exact pack-stage opcode surface but streamed one B column fragment at a time instead of keeping four B fragments live. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=188, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 2 ds_store_b32, 192 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This passes the strict RADV large Q8_0 static contract on the selected opcode/resource axes. After adding the missing catalog route and opt-in selector, focused p512/p513 CPU-reference gates selected this provider for the intended large rows (ffn_out, ffn_gate, result_output, plus p513 tails) and failed with HRX0=inf versus finite CPU values and p512 sentinel mismatches. It is rejected for promotion because the exact static schedule still has incorrect full-pair accumulator lane/output ownership. The next candidate should preserve this stream-column pack-stage schedule while replacing the full-pair writeback mapping with a correctness-proven coordinate map.

The stream-row pack-stage fast-half probe preserved the exact pack-stage opcode surface but kept four B fragments resident and streamed one A row fragment at a time. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=189, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, exactly 128 ds_store_b16, 2 ds_store_b32, 192 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This matches the tracked RADV large Q8_0 static contract while avoiding the stream-column accumulation-order change that caused finite CPU-reference errors. It is still rejected for runtime promotion because it inherits the diagnostic full-pair writeback, and the current row+16 mapping is invalid for gfx11 wave64 WMMA: only the OPSEL-selected accumulator half owns the 16x16 tile output. The next candidate should combine this row-stream issue order with a selected-half correctness gate or a proven full-output lane map before any model-level A/B.

The row-stream selected-half probe combined the pressure-reducing row-stream WMMA issue order with the known-correct selected-half raw buffer-store path. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=189, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. Focused p512 and p513 route traces selected this provider on the intended large Q8_0 rows, while p33 stayed on existing Q8_1 routes and passed. The selected large rows failed strict CPU-reference with finite ERR around 0.0036-0.0039. This refutes row-stream accumulation order under the selected-half output map; the pressure win cannot be promoted without either a Vulkan-equivalent numerical acceptance contract or a different live-range reduction that preserves the non-stream WMMA accumulation order.

The full-tile pack-stage selected probe preserved the non-stream WMMA issue order that passes strict correctness and removed packed input/output edge guards only for exact 128x128-aligned large rows. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=24, VGPR=193, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This lowers the correctness-control pressure from VGPR=196 to VGPR=193 but still misses the RADV 192 ceiling and moves the store surface farther from RADV. Focused p512 CPU-reference passed with route traces selecting the candidate on ffn_out, ffn_gate, and result_output; p33 and p513 were correctly guarded out and passed on existing Q8_1 routes. Same-runner focused perf regressed versus default Q8_1 routes: ffn_out 7031.762 -> 8422.038 us, ffn_gate 6433.416 -> 7332.741 us, result_output 56130.024 -> 64645.333 us. Rejected for promotion.

The named-fragment pack-stage selected probe preserved the strict-correct non-stream A/B load-before-wait and col-then-row WMMA issue order, but spelled the eight A/B fragments as named variables instead of indexed arrays to test whether LLVM kept extra array/index live range. It compiled through CMake/Ninja to the same resource/opcode shape as the indexed selected control: wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. Rejected at compile-evidence gate because it does not move toward the RADV VGPR=192 target or change the emitted schedule.

The Q5_K BHALF packed-Q8_1 probe preserved the current MMQL128 BM128/BN128 wave64 dot issue order while storing Q8_1 RHS d/s in LDS as original half payloads and converting after shared load. The first wrapper build accidentally disabled all accumulation because the shared bquad source had no no-prefetch branch; after adding the default branch it compiled through CMake/Ninja with SGPR=49, VGPR=140, LDS=9728, no spills, wave64, and 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8. Static scoring moved footprint slightly below default but did not improve the local dot window: BHALF scored 12 pre-dot LDS loads, final lgkmcnt=1, and 54 dot ops in the first window versus default 13, 2, and 58. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; route traces selected BHALF only on p512 full-tile rows, while p33 stayed on rows2_cols8 and p513 stayed on the existing MMQL tail path. Focused p512 timing was mixed with a 1.10% four-row sum win, but same-binary Qwen2.5 Coder 7B Q5_K_M p512/fa1 model A/B regressed from 455.164 to 454.457 tok/s with BHALF selected and no fallback. Rejected for gfx1151 promotion; RHS half-scale cache footprint is not the missing parity axis by itself.

The BM128/BN64 split-qsum probe retested row ownership after the accepted BN112/BN128 split-qsum routes proved that qsum live-range splitting can remove the Q8_0 register cliff. The new CMake/Ninja-built route fixed the old BM128/BN64 compile blocker, compiling with wave32, SGPR=22, VGPR=144, LDS=2176, no spills, and private segment 0. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates all passed and route traces selected the opt-in provider. Timing rejects it versus current defaults: p512 total 72.631 ms -> 132.665 ms and p513 total 80.896 ms -> 139.952 ms, with large regressions on ffn_gate and result_output. This closes BM128/BN64 row ownership as a Q8_0 packed-path parity axis despite the fixed compile resource shape.

The pack-stage fast-half selected-output compile probe combined the correctness-proven gfx1151 wave64 D-coordinate map with the low-barrier fast-half LDS output-stage primitive, while still writing and reloading the unselected half as a dummy payload to preserve the halfword LDS opcode surface. It built through CMake/Ninja and compared against the Llama 3.1 8B Q8_0 p512 RADV large oracle with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. It is rejected at compile-contract gate: it does not recover RADV's VGPR=192 pressure, emits only 128 buffer_store_b32 versus RADV's 192, and serializes the first WMMA LDS load window with final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0 and only one ds_load_b64 immediately before the final wait, while RADV keeps 59 ds_load_b64 operations outstanding with final lgkmcnt=51. The selected-half ownership rule is valid, but this HIP C++ spelling does not reproduce the Vulkan cooperative-matrix load/store schedule.

The nowait named-fragment staged-wait probe tested a precise first-WMMA issue-window hypothesis: replace the rejected nowait named-frag route's single zero wait with staged waits at lgkmcnt(12), lgkmcnt(8), lgkmcnt(4), and lgkmcnt(0) before the B-column WMMA groups. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 14 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It is rejected at compile-contract gate because LLVM scheduled the partial waits after the first WMMA group rather than preserving a RADV-like pre-WMMA high-lgkmcnt gate: RADV scores 59 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 59 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 22 WMMA in window; this route scores 24, 0, lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMA in the first-WMMA window, while still lacking the RADV halfword LDS store/load and 192 buffer-store topology.

The nowait named-fragment preuse probe added an empty inline-asm use of all eight A/B fragment vectors before the first wait, testing whether an artificial data dependency can force the fragment LDS loads to materialize before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=212, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 8 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It moved the first-WMMA score in the intended direction versus the prior nowait named-frag route, from 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 / 0 loads immediately before final wait / lgkmcnt=0 to 32 / 32 / lgkmcnt=0. It is rejected because RADV is still 59 / 59 / lgkmcnt=51 with VGPR=192, while this source spelling raises pressure to VGPR=212 and still lacks the RADV halfword LDS store/load and 192 buffer-store topology.

The preuse staged-wait probe combined the prior all-fragment preuse dependency with a wider staged wait ladder at lgkmcnt(24), lgkmcnt(16), lgkmcnt(8), and lgkmcnt(0), testing whether HIP C++ can keep the preuse-created 32-load window partially outstanding before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=212, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 14 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It is rejected at compile-contract gate: the nonzero waits were emitted, but the final pre-WMMA score became 32 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 0 loads immediately before the final wait, final lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMA in the first window. RADV remains 59 / 59 / lgkmcnt=51 / 22 WMMA with VGPR=192 and the halfword LDS plus 192-store topology.

The depwait real-fragment probe ports the accepted CMake WMMA issue-window diagnostic into the real Q8_0 direct-WMMA path by copying real A/B fragments through dependency-pinned inline asm and emitting a RADV-like wait ladder. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=240, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 38 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The compile contract preserves final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=51 and the wait ladder, but the real-fragment source only presents one k_tile at a time, so the first-WMMA score is 32 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 and 32 loads immediately before the final wait rather than RADV's 59 and 59, while VGPR pressure rises to 240 versus RADV's 192. After selected-lane WMMA diagnostics proved odd accumulator halves should not veto the full 4x4 shape, the route was wired as an opt-in runtime probe and passed focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates. Route traces showed p33 stayed on BN64 and p512/p513 selected the depwait route only for the intended large rows. Same-runner focused timing still rejected it versus current packed-Q8_1 defaults: p512 total 71977.24 -> 101026.76 us and p513 total 81449.83 -> 116681.09 us, with the dominant large FFN/output rows regressing about 30%. Keep it as a diagnostic selector only.

The two-K-tile depwait probe forced both VK128 K tiles' A/B fragments live before the first WMMA, mechanically testing whether HIP C++ can reach RADV's 59-load pre-WMMA issue window in the real non-stream selected-half Q8_0 path. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The first-WMMA schedule score improves substantially versus the one-tile depwait route: 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before the final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. It is still rejected at compile-contract gate because RADV is 59/59/lgkmcnt=51 with VGPR=192 and no spills, while this HIP C++ spelling creates a hard register cliff and still lacks RADV's 128 ds_store_b16, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, and 192 buffer_store_b32 cooperative writeback topology.

The two-K-tile no-preuse depwait probe preserved the K2 source-visible A/B fragment loads and RADV-like wait ladder, but disabled the explicit empty inline-asm preuse of all 16 loaded fragments. This mechanically tested whether the K2 register cliff came from the artificial preuse dependency rather than from exposing both K tiles before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja and emitted the same tracked contract as the original K2 route: wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, 44 s_waitcnt_depctr, first-WMMA score 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. Rejected before runtime because removing the explicit preuse does not reduce pressure or improve the issue window; the live-range cliff is inherent to this source-level two-K fragment exposure.

The two-K-tile direct-wait probe preserved the K2 preload shape but removed the dependency-copy v_mov path, issuing direct WMMA calls with explicit RADV-like wait counts. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=196, no spills, private segment=0, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, and 37 s_waitcnt. This proves the K2 register cliff is caused by the dependency-copy machinery, not by the two-K source variables alone. It is still rejected at compile-contract gate because the compiler collapses the first-WMMA issue window back to 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, zero loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMAs in the first window. RADV remains 59/59/lgkmcnt=51/22 with VGPR=192 and no spills.

The two-K-tile raw-fragment depwait probe preserved the K2 RADV-like wait ladder but loaded both K tiles as raw u64x4 LDS fragments, casting to half16 only at the WMMA boundary. This mechanically tested whether the K2 spill cliff was caused by the half16 vector representation rather than by exposing both K tiles and dependency-copying operands. It built through CMake/Ninja with the same tracked pressure contract as the original K2 depwait route: wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The first-WMMA score stays in the K2 neighborhood, with 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. Rejected before runtime because raw fragment representation does not reduce pressure or recover RADV's no-spill 192-VGPR contract, 59/59 issue window, or halfword LDS/writeback topology.

The B-stripe compile-contract probe preserved the accepted BM64/BN128 split-qsum route and explicitly preloaded each 16-column B-cache iqs stripe before dot consumption to test whether source-visible B issue ordering can change the packed path's first-dot schedule. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=152, LDS=4352, no spills, 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8 sites, and the exact same first-hot-op score as accepted BN128 split-qsum: 28 pre-hot loads, final lgkmcnt=14, and 60 hot ops. Rejected before runtime because it does not change the emitted schedule or resource contract; future Q8_0 packed work needs a materially different issue/window primitive or lower-level path, not local B-cache staging spelling.

DeepSeek R1 Qwen 14B Q4_K_M p512 remained below Vulkan despite accepted Q4 B-quad routing, so the embedded Q6_K prompt rows were isolated as a selector-policy probe. Exported DeepSeek Q6 rows Vcur-0, ffn_out-0, and result_output all passed CPU-reference with the current Q6 VK128 WMMA default and with the rollback path. Route traces showed the default selected hrx_mul_mat_vec_q6_k_wmma16x16_vk128_padded_w64_f16acc_wg256_f32 for all focused rows, while rollback selected rows2_cols8 for Vcur and q8_1_x4_mmql64x128 for ffn_out/result_output. Same-runner focused p512 timing rejects rollback decisively: Vcur 1450.68 -> 2939.99 us, ffn_out 24145.94 -> 198921.26 us, and result_output 292046.56 -> 2199564.33 us. The DeepSeek gap is not fixed by undoing the accepted Q6 large WMMA selector; future work should target a materially different Q6 schedule primitive or another measured boulder.

The Q5_K VK128 packstage+fast-half selected-store probe ports the Q8_0 direct-WMMA diagnostic controls into the Q5 source family: ds_write_b32 A/B pack staging, B64GROUP LDS fragment reads, selected-half LDS b16 store/load, and raw buffer stores. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=37, VGPR=199, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 barriers. This mechanically reaches the RADV large-route LDS and halfword topology axes that previous Q5 bufferstore probes missed, but focused p512 CPU-reference failed on all four Q5 rows with large finite error: Kcur ERR 1.9417, Qcur ERR 3.9573, ffn_out ERR 3.9666, and ffn_gate ERR 3.8717. Route traces confirmed p33 correctly stayed on existing rows2/VK64 policy and p512 selected the candidate. Reject before perf/model testing: the selected-half accumulator store/lane mapping is not semantically valid for Q5 in this HIP C++ spelling, and the route still emits 128 rather than RADV's 192 buffer_store_b32.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 H4LOAD probe preserved the accepted p33 medium-route clone's BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64/11264-byte-LDS contract and changed LDS fragment reads from scalar half indexing to half4 chunk loads. This directly tested whether source-visible half4 reads could move the accepted narrow route toward the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium topology: 16 WMMA sites, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 64 LDS b16 stores, and 96 buffer stores. It built through CMake/Ninja but is compile-equivalent to the accepted VK64 route for the tracked facts: wave64, SGPR=36, VGPR=59, LDS=11264, no spills, 8 visible v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 20 ds_load_2addr_b64, 0 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_u16_d16, 2 ds_store_b16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, and 58 s_waitcnt. Reject before runtime timing; this local HIP C++ load spelling does not expose the missing RADV cooperative load/store topology.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 GROUPK2 probe changed the live fragment topology instead of just changing source load syntax: each wave preloads both K tiles' four A fragments plus one B fragment through nowait b64 LDS reads before issuing the eight WMMAs. This mechanically targeted RADV's p33 medium issue window, where 48 ds_load_b64 appear before the first WMMA with final lgkmcnt(40) and 16 WMMAs in the first window. The compile contract moved in the intended direction versus accepted VK64: wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=101, LDS=11264, no spills, 40 ds_load_b64, 8 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 barriers, 10 s_waitcnt, and 41 s_waitcnt_depctr. However, the scored first window only had 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, final lgkmcnt(0), and 8 WMMAs, still short of RADV. Focused p33 CPU-reference failed all three rows with NaNs while route traces confirmed GROUPK2 selection. p512 and p513 non-steal CPU-reference gates passed and stayed on the existing VK128 provider. Reject before timing/model tests; the simple grouped nowait preload is not a correct substitute for RADV's cooperative load/WMMA schedule.

The GROUPK2_WAIT probe kept GROUPK2's two-K grouped fragment topology but replaced nowait b64 fragment reads with the existing per-load wait helper to isolate whether GROUPK2's NaNs were a wait/dependency issue or a lane/fragment mapping issue. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=101, LDS=11264, no spills, 40 ds_load_b64, 8 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 barriers, 50 s_waitcnt, and 41 s_waitcnt_depctr. The scored first window remained far from RADV: 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, final lgkmcnt(0), and only 4 WMMAs in the first-WMMA window versus RADV's 48/lgkmcnt(40)/16. Focused p33 CPU-reference selected the route and changed the failure mode from NaNs to finite mismatch: Vcur passed, ffn_out failed with ERR 0.001619838, and result_output failed with ERR 0.007942211. p512 and p513 non-steal gates passed and stayed on VK128. Reject before timing/model testing; the missing schedule cannot be recovered by simply adding per-load waits to the grouped scalar-fragment preload.

This probe preserved the accepted Q5_K VK64 padded44 wave64 narrow FFN-gate schedule and changed only the full-tile writeback policy. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=75, LDS=11264, private segment=0, and no spills. Focused CPU-reference passed for p33 and p512/p513 non-steal gates; p33 route traces selected the fullstore provider only for the k=3584 rows=18944 cols=33 FFN gate/up slice, while p512/p513 stayed on rows2 plus MMQL128 routes. Initial focused timing improved ffn_gate 1797.31 -> 1758.83 us and repeated model A/B improved Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 steady tok/s 169.717 -> 171.064. However, post-edit same-runner focused timing was mixed: one pass regressed ffn_gate 1827.65 -> 1864.51 us, while the rerun improved ffn_gate 1821.96 -> 1810.51 us with noisy neighboring rows. A current-head r9 rerun kept the model-level signal small but positive, 170.072 -> 171.744 steady tok/s, and route traces confirmed 486 dispatches switched from the accepted VK64 narrow provider to fullstore. The decisive focused rerun remained flat/noisy: Kcur 71.865 -> 74.072 us, Qcur 259.392 -> 259.291 us, ffn_out 1537.784 -> 1532.410 us, and ffn_gate 1716.238 -> 1717.690 us. Reject for default promotion because the focused kernel evidence does not show a durable target-row win; keep opt-in as a diagnostic writeback-axis probe.

The Q5_K VK64 combined96 probe transplanted the standalone p33 medium fixture into the real direct-F32 Q5 wrapper as a p33-only opt-in catalog route. It built through CMake/Ninja and preserved the main RADV p33 total surface better than prior VK64 probes: wave64, LDS=11264, private segment=0, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, and 96 buffer_store_b32. However, the real ABI schedule did not preserve the fixture's issue window: static compare against RADV aligned_m showed SGPR=55 versus 108, VGPR=142 versus 144, 66 ds_store_b16 versus 64, 4 barriers versus 2, only 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 versus 48, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt(0) versus 40. Focused p33 CPU-reference selected the combined96 route for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M rows and failed all four with NaNs. Reject before timing/model tests; the catalog port proves the opcode-count surface is reachable in the real ABI, but lane ownership and compiler scheduling still need a lower-level dependency/lane-mapping reproducer before another production promotion attempt.

The Q5_K VK64 full64 probe repaired the combined96 output-ownership bug by computing all 16 medium-tile output groups in wave0 and writing only groups 0..15. It built through CMake/Ninja and selected for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 focused rows, but CPU-reference failed all four with NaNs. A follow-up CMake-built lane-map fixture, hrx-hip-bench-wmma-f16-lane-map --mode=full64-store-contract, proved the full64 coordinate contract itself is valid for cols 32, 33, and 64: all target cells were written exactly once with no NaNs. Additional CMake-built WMMA/LDS fixtures narrowed the failure: one-K, two-K, and production stride44 LDS-fed fragment probes can produce NaNs in inactive odd accumulator slots, and per-load lgkmcnt waits do not clear those inactive-slot NaNs, but the selected even output slots remain finite in the generic, long-repeat, and production-stride fixtures. A final CMake-built exact-kernel reproducer, hrx-hip-bench-q5-wmma-full64-repro, launched the actual full64 catalog kernel with synthetic Q5 dequant data and reproduced selected-output NaNs. The small-scale profile reproduced p33 NaNs with no Infs for rows=64, cols=33, k=256/512/3584, so this is not just a stress-scale F16 overflow artifact. Reduced-active-group variants using the same Q5 dequant, stride44 LDS staging, b64 fragment loads, and full64 store contract further bracketed the failure: active1 and active4 were finite, active8 was finite but badly wrong, and active12/active16 reproduced selected-output NaNs. A batched4 full-output diagnostic then computed all sixteen output groups four at a time; it was finite for the p33 small-scale case and matched the active4 error scale. Therefore the failure requires the exact Q5 dequant/shared-layout source context plus the high live-accumulator full64 topology; it is not explained by missing/duplicate output coordinates, simple LDS wait placement, or stride44 fragment loads alone. Static compare against the p33 RADV medium oracle still shows this is not a viable schedule clone: SGPR=64 versus 108, VGPR=198 versus 144, LDS=11264, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 versus 16, 64 ds_load_b64 versus 48, 64 buffer_store_b32 versus 96, no ds_load_u16_d16 store stage, 3 barriers versus 2, only 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 in the scored first window, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt(0) instead of RADV lgkmcnt(40). Reject before timing/model tests; the HIP builtin/register allocation for 12+ live f16 WMMA accumulators is outside the useful schedule family. The next candidate should use low live-accumulator group batching or a closer RADV cooperative staging/writeback spelling, not a monolithic full64 accumulator set.

The Q5_K VK64 batched4 catalog probe moved the finite exact-kernel diagnostic into an opt-in p33 route: BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64, full medium-tile output ownership, but only four live f16 WMMA accumulator groups at a time. It built through CMake/Ninja; the selected batched4 export reports SGPR=51, VGPR=186, LDS=11264, private segment=0, no spills, and wavefront_size=64. The HSACO also contains the included full64 helper export, but route traces select the batched4 export by name. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M rows with route evidence, proving that low live-accumulator batching avoids the full64 selected-output NaNs in the real catalog ABI. Same-runner focused timing rejects it as a production schedule: Kcur 72.754 -> 1386.552 us, Qcur 259.498 -> 1771.570 us, ffn_out 1535.251 -> 12762.069 us, and ffn_gate 1715.737 -> 8246.900 us. The selected-symbol ISA explains the loss: 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 256 ds_load_b64, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 12 barriers versus RADV p33 medium's 16 WMMA, 48 ds_load_b64, 96 buffer stores, and 2 barriers. Reject before model tests. Keep the correctness conclusion, but the next candidate must preserve low live accumulator pressure without restaging A/B four times; a closer RADV cooperative staging/writeback spelling is still required.

The Q5_K VK64 wave4row probe tested the obvious next pivot after batched4: keep BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64 and full medium-tile ownership, but map the four waves in the workgroup to the four 16-row stripes so each wave keeps only four live f16 WMMA accumulators while A/B are staged once per K tile. The initial nowait LDS fragment-load spelling selected for all focused p33 rows but failed CPU-reference with finite errors on Kcur/Qcur/ffn_gate and one NaN on ffn_out, proving the multi-wave shape needs explicit fragment-load waits. The waited spelling built through CMake/Ninja and passed all four focused Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 rows with route evidence. Its selected export reports wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=102, LDS=11264, private segment=0, no spills, 8 visible v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 40 ds_load_b64, 16 buffer_store_b32, 2 barriers, and 51 s_waitcnt. This is the closest HIP C++ p33 medium compile contract so far, but same-runner focused timing still rejects it: Kcur 72.210 -> 398.540 us, Qcur 259.574 -> 474.473 us, ffn_out 1538.760 -> 3406.255 us, and ffn_gate 1721.514 -> 2380.085 us. Reject before model tests. The evidence says all-wave low-live WMMA can be made correct and avoids the batched4 restage explosion, but direct-F32 WMMA still loses to the accepted rows2/cols8 path; the next Q5 p33 route needs either a closer RADV cooperative store/fragment contract or a packed-Q8_1 medium schedule rather than another direct-F32 WMMA ownership reshuffle.

The Q5_K VK64 batched4-p33 probe moved the standalone p33-pruned batched4 diagnostic into an opt-in catalog route. It preserved the exact full batched4 source topology for groups 0..11 and skipped only the unused group_base=12 phase. It built through CMake/Ninja and selected for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 focused rows. CPU-reference passed Kcur, Qcur, and ffn_gate but failed ffn_out at k=18944 rows=3584 cols=33 with finite ERR=0.043113960, so the standalone correctness result at k=256/k=3584 did not generalize to the wide-K focused row. Selected-symbol HSACO facts matched the native repro: wave64, SGPR=51, VGPR=182, LDS=11264, private segment=0, no spills, 24 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 192 ds_load_b64, 48 buffer_store_b32, 9 barriers, and 80 s_waitcnt. Reject before timing/model tests. The full four-phase batched4 route remains the direct-WMMA correctness oracle for p33 wide-K; simple p33 phase pruning is not a safe catalog route.

rejections.reason: The Q5_K VK64 narrow FFN route was originally defaulted because it beat the rows2 direct-F32 fallback on the exact Qwen2.5 Coder p33 ffn_gate shape. After the packed Q8_1/x4 MMQL64 BK2 BQUAD route became the narrow default, a selector-only A/B showed that the old direct default was now shadowing a faster packed path on the same k=3584 rows=18944 cols=33 row. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed with the old route disabled, p512 and p513 non-steal correctness stayed on the existing large/tail packed routes, and route traces showed ffn_gate moving from VK64 narrow to BQUAD. Same-runner focused timing improved ffn_gate 1711.823 -> 1156.896 us with Kcur/Qcur/ffn_out flat, and same-binary Qwen2.5 Coder 7B Q5_K_M p33/fa1 model throughput improved 170.239 -> 209.917 tok/s. Supersede the VK64 narrow default and keep it opt-in only as a direct-WMMA diagnostic; further Q5 p33 parity work should start from the packed medium route or a true RADV cooperative lane/store clone.

The Q5_K packed-Q8_1/x4 MMQL64 BK2 B-pair probe bracketed the accepted p33 BQUAD route by preserving BM64/BN64/BK_STEP=2/WG256/wave64 and changing only the B-cache live window from a full WNITER x TN B-quad to one TN-wide pair per WNITER. It built through CMake/Ninja, and focused CPU-reference passed for p33 plus p512/p513 non-steal guards. Route traces proved p33 selected B-pair for Qcur, ffn_out, and ffn_gate while Kcur stayed on rows2; p512 stayed on MMQL128 and p513 stayed on MMQL128 BQUAD tail. Static HSACO comparison showed the intended pressure reduction, wave64 SGPR=62 VGPR=105 LDS=10240 no spills, versus BQUAD VGPR=124 with the same LDS, 256 v_dot sites, 40 ds_load, 24 ds_store, 39 global_load, 16 global_store, and 2 barriers. Same-runner focused timing rejected the route despite lower VGPR: round 1 p33 sum regressed 3071.563 -> 3144.005 us and round 2 regressed 3067.537 -> 3145.376 us. The ffn_out row slightly improved, but Qcur regressed about 2.2% and ffn_gate regressed about 7.5%, so reducing the B live window is not the right packed-medium axis for Q5 p33. Keep BQUAD as the accepted default and keep this B-pair route opt-in only as rejection evidence.

The Q5_K packed-Q8_1/x4 MMQL64 BK2 TN4/BQUAD probe preserved the accepted p33 BQUAD route's BM64/BN64/BK_STEP=2/WG256/wave64 dataflow and BQUAD issue window, but changed per-lane output ownership from TM4/TN2 to TM2/TN4. This was a bounded packed-RHS/output-ownership axis after BK1, B-pair, B-quad, and CR-major issue order had already been tested. It built through CMake/Ninja but failed the compile-resource gate before runtime tests: wave64 SGPR=62, VGPR=192, VGPR spills=183, private_segment_fixed_size=736, LDS=10240. For comparison, the accepted BQUAD route is wave64 SGPR=62, VGPR=124, no spills, private_segment_fixed_size=0, LDS=10240. TN4 preserves 256 v_dot sites and two barriers but raises ds_load count from 40 to 50 and s_waitcnt count from 119 to 249. Reject before focused correctness/perf; the TN4 ownership pivot hits the gfx1151 register cliff and is not a viable packed-medium schedule.

rejections.route: hrx-hip-bench-q8-wmma-repro diagnostic modes bfrag-dump, single-group8-bmirror0, and single-group12-bmirror0
rejections.reason: The Q8_0 WMMA repro added a B-fragment dump that stages RHS through the same padded LDS layout and loads all four B column fragments with the production ds_read_b64 helper. It passed exactly for cols=64 and cols=33: active=8192, bad=0, nan=0, sentinel=0, max_abs=0. This clears raw upper-column B-fragment load values, including the odd p33 edge. The follow-up bmirror modes mirrored lower-column RHS values into the upper B column tiles, then computed through the upper col_sub paths and compared against lower-column CPU reference values. Both upper paths still failed: group8 reported p64 bad=256 nan=96 max_abs=16976 and p33 bad=16 nan=8 max_abs=5484; group12 reported p64 bad=256 nan=0 max_abs=12.9951. Static device evidence stayed small and non-spilling: bmirror group8 wave64 SGPR=40 VGPR=99 LDS=10240, bmirror group12 wave64 SGPR=32 VGPR=110 LDS=10240, each with 2 WMMA, 64 ds_load_b64, 4 buffer_store_b32, and 2 barriers. Reject the hypothesis that distinct upper-column RHS data or raw B-fragment loads explain the upper-column failure. The remaining blocker is the upper B operand slot/register/WMMA consumption contract in this HIP C++ spelling; the next probe should change operand materialization or use a lower-level WMMA operand spelling, not retest B-value staging.

rejections.route: hrx-hip-bench-q8-wmma-repro diagnostic modes single-group*-bcopy, single-group*-abcopy, array8-fullb-2phase-bcopy, and array8-fullb-2phase-abcopy
rejections.reason: The Q8_0 WMMA repro added an explicit v_mov_b32 fragment materialization helper to test the upper B operand slot/register failure isolated by the bfrag/bmirror probes. Single-group upper-column modes passed after materialization: group8 B-copy p64/p33 bad=0 max_abs=0.109412/0.0129853, group8 A+B-copy p64/p33 bad=0 max_abs=0.00288854/0.00212485, group12 B-copy p64 bad=0 max_abs=0.132035, and group12 A+B-copy p64 bad=0 max_abs=0.00239494. The repair also survived the full two-phase topology that previously failed groups 0/1/8/9: B-copy p64/p33 bad=0 max_abs=0.109595/0.108497 and A+B-copy p64/p33 bad=0 max_abs=0.00268994/0.00262882. This is accepted as a correctness primitive but rejected as a production spelling as-is: single-group copies raise VGPR to 117, while full two-phase B-copy reaches VGPR=235 with 219 v_mov_b32 per phase and A+B-copy reaches VGPR=247 with 347 v_mov_b32 per phase. The next production candidate should apply the narrowest materialization needed, likely B-only or upper-column-only, and must pass focused route/static/timing gates before any model-level promotion.

The split-selected B-copy route tested whether the standalone Q8_0 fragment-copy repair transfers into the real large direct-WMMA catalog ABI. The upper-only transfer built and selected for the p512 ffn_out, ffn_gate, and result_output rows but failed CPU-reference with ffn_out ERR=3.007032931, ffn_gate ERR=1.773888636, and result_output NaN at index 6188064. The route was then pivoted to full B-copy to match the passing array8-fullb-2phase-bcopy repro more closely. Full B-copy compiled through CMake/Ninja as wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=212, LDS=22528, no private segment, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 128 buffer_store_b32, two barriers, and 199 waitcnt-class instructions. Focused p512 route traces again proved Vcur and Qcur stayed on the packed Q8_1 provider while ffn_out, ffn_gate, and result_output selected the B-copy provider; the selected rows still failed with ffn_out ERR=2.699209606, ffn_gate ERR=2.588006472, and result_output NaN at index 6188064. Reject before timing/model tests. The fragment-copy primitive repairs the small standalone full-two-phase topology, but it does not repair the production split-selected route, likely because the remaining invalid surface is selected-half accumulator writeback or broader WMMA lane ownership rather than just B operand materialization.
